title: Resilient Constrained Learning
authors: Ignacio Hounie, Alejandro Ribeiro, Luiz F. O. Chamon
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS), vol. 36
issues: none -- title/authors/venue/volume/year all verified against the PDF front matter and NeurIPS 2023 (vol. 36) proceeding. The Related-Work description ('adapts the constraint level to make hard requirements attainable') matches the paper's own framing (Def. 1 resilient equilibrium, Prop. 3/4 Lagrangian reformulation) precisely, and characterizing the algorithm as 'dual-ascent' is accurate since Algorithm 1 performs projected gradient ascent on the Lagrange multipliers lambda. our_use: Cited three times as one of the 'two strongest dual-ascent' constraint-TRAINED baselines ('Hounie-RCL') that TraLO is compared against on the transductive count-cap task (main.tex ~L92, ~L172, ~L356: 'Two constraint-trained dual-ascent methods: Fioretto-LDF ... and Hounie-RCL'). Also cited in Related Work (~L156) with the accurate characterization 'Resilient Constrained Learning adapts the constraint level to make hard requirements attainable', contrasted with TraLO's bounded-penalty/frozen-multiplier approach. conclusions: Introduces 'resilient constrained learning': instead of fixing hard constraint levels u_i=0, the method jointly solves the learning problem and adapts each constraint's relaxation u_i, trading the objective loss against a user-defined relaxation cost h(u). | Defines the 'resilient equilibrium' (an equilibrium between the marginal decrease in loss and the marginal increase in relaxation cost) and proves existence/uniqueness under convexity of the perturbation function. | Shows the resilient problem is equivalent to a Lagrangian/dual reformulation, giving a practical primal-dual (dual-ascent) algorithm (Alg. 1) that updates model params, per-constraint relaxations u, and Lagrange multipliers lambda by (projected) gradient ascent/descent each step. | Provides finite-sample approximation/generalization bounds (Thm. 1) for the empirical resilient dual problem. | Empirically validated on two tasks: heterogeneous federated learning under class imbalance (relaxes the harder, minority-heavy clients' proximity constraints more, improving most clients' accuracy) and invariance-constrained learning on MNIST/Fashion-MNIST (relaxes constraints for transformations that are not true invariances, improving test accuracy over both constrained and unconstrained baselines). | The paper's own tasks are class-imbalance-aware federated fairness and augmentation/invariance constraints -- NOT a transductive, hard-cap test-set prediction-count problem; the multiplier/relaxation machinery is the general-purpose part our paper borrows and re-instantiates on the count-cap task.

issues: none -- title, author list, venue (37th ICML / PMLR vol. 119), page range (9133-9143), publisher (PMLR), and year (2020) all verified against the PDF front matter and cross-checked against the PMLR proceedings page (proceedings.mlr.press/v119/stooke20a.html). our_use: main.tex:150-158 (Related Work, 'Lagrangian and dual constrained learning' paragraph): '...and PID-style dual updates stabilize the multiplier in safe RL \citep{stooke2020responsive}...' -- cited as an example, from the adjacent safe-RL literature, of techniques that stabilize/dampen the Lagrange multiplier's update dynamics, paralleling our own multiplier-stabilization mechanisms (ratchet-then-freeze, optimizer reset).
conclusions: Traditional Lagrangian methods for constrained (safe) RL update the multiplier by pure integral control, which produces oscillations and cost overshoot/violations during training. | The paper reinterprets the Lagrange multiplier update as a control-theory problem and adds proportional and derivative terms (PID control) to the standard integral-only update. | Proportional control (PI-control) damps oscillations and improves robustness to the integral learning rate K_I across multiple Safety Gym environments (DoggoGoal, DoggoButton, CarButton, PointGoal). | Derivative control further prevents cost overshoot and slows the approach to the constraint boundary, acting predictively rather than reactively. | A complementary reward/cost scale-invariance technique (beta-weighting of the policy gradient) makes controller tuning transferable across differently-scaled reward/cost objectives. | CPPO (PID-Lagrangian applied to PPO) sets a new state of the art on the Safety Gym benchmark, improving the return-vs-constraint-violation Pareto frontier over the plain Lagrangian baseline.

The characterization 'output-layer satisfiability solver' accurately reflects the paper's last-layer MaxSMT mechanism, and 'guaranteed per prediction by construction' accurately reflects its universally-quantified, by-construction guarantee (as opposed to our bounded soft penalty). One minor nuance for the authors to be aware of (not a bibliography error): DeepSaDe's guarantee is over per-instance logical constraints on a bounded domain, not a dataset-level/transductive count constraint like TraLO's -- but our sentence does not claim otherwise, it only lists it as an alternative mechanism for guaranteeing constraint satisfaction.
our_use: main.tex:163-166 (related-work paragraph on prior mechanisms for enforcing output constraints): '...guaranteed per prediction by construction through input-dependent parametrizations \citep{brosowsky2021sample} or an output-layer satisfiability solver \citep{goyal2024deepsade}; \citet{marquez2017imposing} find hard enforcement feasible but no better than soft penalties, which motivates our bounded penalty.' The citation is used purely as one example of a training-time, by-construction hard-guarantee mechanism (contrasted with our soft/bounded transductive penalty), not claimed to solve the same transductive count-cap problem.
conclusions: DeepSaDe enforces universally-quantified logical domain constraints (if x satisfies P then f(x) must satisfy C) over a bounded input domain, guaranteeing satisfaction for ALL inputs in that domain, not just training examples. | The guarantee is achieved training-time, at the network's last (output) layer: each batch update solves a MaxSMT (Maximum Satisfiability Modulo Theories, via the Z3 solver) problem to pick last-layer weights that satisfy the constraint set, falling back to a faster line search first; earlier layers still use ordinary gradient descent. | This gives per-instance/by-construction guarantees rather than a soft penalty: the network is only accepted/updated when the constraint holds, so violation is structurally impossible after each step. | Empirically DeepSaDe reaches 100% constraint accuracy (zero counterexamples, AdI=0) on five constrained-learning use cases, versus regularization baselines that leave exploitable counterexamples (e.g. one baseline at 93.5% constraint accuracy with counterexamples near 97% of instances). | The guarantee has a large computational cost: 10x-500x more training time than unconstrained/regularization baselines, attributed to the MaxSMT solving overhead; predictive accuracy is comparable to baselines on most use cases. | The constraints handled are per-instance logical/numerical relationships (sums, ratios, inequalities, disjunctions/conjunctions), not dataset-level or transductive aggregate-count constraints like the caps used in our paper.
